## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical enforcement of attestation for edge modules, including SBOM integration and automation.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign signing and attestations
- SBOMs for wasm modules
- Runtime admission controls (Kyverno/OPA)
- GitHub Actions automation

## Code Example

```bash
cosign sign --key cosign.key ghcr.io/org/module@tag
cosign attest --predicate attest.json --signature sig.cosign ghcr.io/org/module@tag
```

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-attested-wasm
spec:
  rules:
  - name: attestation-check
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            app: wasm-edge
    validate:
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "ghcr.io/org/*"
            securityContext:
              capabilities:
                add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]
  - name: verify-attestation
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      anyPattern:
      - pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              cosign.sigstore.dev/attestations: "?*"
```

- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- NetworkPolicy default deny and cross-namespace access

## Code Example
```javascript
function checkManifest(m) {
  const cs = m?.spec?.template?.spec?.containers?.every(c => c.securityContext?.runAsNonRoot === true && c.securityContext?.runAsUser === 1000);
  const ro = m?.spec?.template?.spec?.containers?.every(c => c?.securityContext?.readOnlyRootFilesystem === true);
  return cs && ro;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical security controls: CI image signing, tag governance, and runtime enforcement with Kyverno; it requires understanding Cosign, Rekor, image verification, and policy-as-code interplay, plus how to craft minimal manifests and verify locally, in CI, and at runtime.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Tag policy regex
- Kyverno image verification at admission
- Minimal manifest testing (unsigned vs signed)
- CI and runtime integration and trade-offs (latency, private registries)

## Code Example

```yaml
# CI workflow snippet (Cosign verify)
name: CI Image Sign Check
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          cosign verify registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signed-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validateImages:
      - image: "*"
        cosign:
          publicKey: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            ...
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (unsigned image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ride-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (signed image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ride-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0-signed
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle private registries and key rotation in Cosign?
- What are trade-offs of enforcing signatures at admission vs. build-time validations?
- How would you scale this policy across dozens of namespaces and clusters?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of container security in CI for beginner level, with concrete commands and outcomes.

## Key Concepts
- Trivy usage; severity filters
- CI gate semantics; exit codes
- Image vs filesystem scan; chart scanning

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Security gate
on: [push]
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v4
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          tags: myservice:latest
      - name: Trivy image
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v2
        with:
          image: myservice:latest
          severity: HIGH
          exit-code: 1
      - name: Trivy charts
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v2
        with:
          directory: "charts"
          severity: HIGH
          exit-code: 1
```

## Why This Is Asked
GPU ML clusters rely on kernel modules from a private registry; enforcing integrity at load time is critical to prevent tampering.

## Key Concepts
- cosign signing and Rekor attestations
- load-time attestation verification
- policy enforcement via OPA/Kyverno

## Code Example
```bash
cosign sign -key cosign.key path/to/module.ko
cosign sign -key cosign.key path/to/module.json
cosign verify path/to/module.ko
```

```bash
# OPA snippet
package kernel.authz

violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.attestation.subject == "module.ko"
  not input.attestation.issuer in ["approved-issuer-A","approved-issuer-B"]
  msg := "unapproved module attestation"
}
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (simplified)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata: { name: attested-modules }
spec:
  rules:
  - id: require-attested-modules
    match: { any: [{ context: { name: "kernel-loader" } }] }
    validate:
      message: "Module must be attested"
      pattern:
        any: true
```

- How would you test this policy at scale without affecting running workloads?
